methodology_and_interpretation.sample_peak: Maximum decoded sample amplitude, expressed in dBFS.
methodology_and_interpretation.rms: Whole-file RMS signal level, expressed in dBFS; this is not a perceptual loudness measurement.
methodology_and_interpretation.near_full_scale_counter: The analyzer counts samples with absolute normalized amplitude >= 0.999 (approximately -0.01 dBFS). This is a near-full-scale counter, not proof of hard clipping.
methodology_and_interpretation.integrated_loudness: FFmpeg loudnorm EBU R128 analysis pass; read-only measurement, not normalization.
methodology_and_interpretation.loudness_range: LRA measured by the EBU R128 loudness analysis pass.
methodology_and_interpretation.true_peak: True-peak estimate measured by the EBU R128 loudness analysis pass.
methodology_and_interpretation.near_silence: Share of 100 ms windows below -55 dBFS RMS. These regions may be intentional horror pauses and are not automatically defects.

interpretation: Both latest final mix WAV files were decoded and inspected successfully by the local analyzer.
The latest near-full-scale sample counter is zero for both mixes.
The Hindi integrated loudness is -23.72 LUFS and the English integrated loudness is -24.34 LUFS, a 0.62 LU difference.
The Hindi true peak is -0.88 dBTP and the English true peak is -1.20 dBTP.
The Hindi LRA is 17.60 LU; the English LRA is 12.20 LU. These values indicate different loudness dynamics; they do not independently establish dialogue intelligibility or mix quality.
No objective dialogue-versus-music separation measurement or listening-based quality approval is included in this snapshot.
